prompt: Some people think that parents should teach their children how to be good members of society. Others, however, believe that school is the best place to learn this. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
There is an ongoing debate over whether parents or schools should be primarily responsible for teaching children to become good members of society. While parents play an important role in shaping their children’s behaviour, I believe that schools have a greater responsibility because they teach young people how to interact and cooperate with others outside their family.

Parents can strongly influence their children’s behaviour by acting as role models. Since children often look up to their parents, they tend to observe and copy the way they behave. Young children, in particular, may imitate not only their parents’ actions but also the way they speak to other people. For example, if parents consistently speak politely to others and help people in need, their children are likely to follow their example and develop values such as respect and compassion. In this way, children’s behaviour can be shaped by what they see at home, meaning that parents have an important part to play in helping them develop positive attitudes towards others.

Schools, on the other hand, have a broader influence because students spend a significant amount of time there and regularly interact with people from different backgrounds. Every school has its own rules and expectations, which students are required to follow in order to get along with their classmates and teachers. This gives them opportunities to practise cooperation, respect and other social skills in situations that are different from those at home. For example, students in Thailand often have to complete group projects in science classes. By working together to complete a task, they learn how to share responsibilities, listen to different opinions and solve problems with others. These skills can be useful later in life, when they have to work with people in universities, workplaces and wider communities. Therefore, schools play a significant role in preparing young people to become responsible members of society.

In conclusion, although parents’ behaviour can have a lasting effect on their children’s character, I believe schools have a greater influence because they provide young people with regular opportunities to interact, cooperate and learn how to behave appropriately in a wider social environment.
